rows.claim: A modification is not done until a named capability battery reruns green, and the verification stage is copied even when the modification itself is rejected; OBLITERATUS proves the discipline in someone else's forge (EXCISE then VERIFY capability retention before REBIRTH/save).
rows.quote:
The verification stage (capability retention check) is the part to copy
  regardless of whether we adopt the ablation: verify-after-modify with a
  named battery is our own gate discipline, proven in someone else's forge.
rows.steal: One seat one sitting: before wiring any quantize/abliterate/convert rung into the janitor ladder, land the named battery first (fleet scut battery + probe20 pairs, FKB refusal census) and make the rung's gate read battery-green-or-no-land (refusals drop, no task-success regression, probe20 drift pairs flat); landing spot: the P1 probe in queue/todo.md and the quantizer gate path.
rows.falsifier: A modified model or mechanism is claimed done with the named battery skipped, run after the claim, or swapped for an unnamed ad hoc check, and no gate blocks the claim.

rows.law: Ouroboros self-repair detection: excise at one layer, watch downstream
rows.claim: After excising a behavior at one layer, keep a detector watching for its re-emergence downstream; a fix that can be silently re-encoded is displaced, not closed, and the detector is the measurement that tells the difference.
rows.quote:
their module is the measurement shape to steal: excise a
   behavior at one layer, detect its re-emergence downstream.
rows.steal: One seat one sitting: for every violation class the ratchet/prune removes, keep its detector alive post-fix (violation_ratchet and census_drift_patrol stay enabled after prune, drift_check watches re-landing of an excised pattern in new shapes); landing spot: tools/violation_ratchet.py prune workflow plus the drift-patrol config, one class per sitting.
rows.falsifier: A class excised at layer A re-appears downstream in a new file or shape and no detector fires for multiple patrol cycles.

rows.law: isError in-band failure is the hook of conditional composition
rows.claim: Tools report their own failures inside the result object so the caller can branch; conditional composition is possible because failure arrives as data the next turn can read, not as transport death, and protocol-level errors carry no recovery path.
rows.quote: the agent can branch on failure because failure arrives as data, not as transport death.
rows.steal: One seat one sitting: audit one estate tool wrapper for exceptions that escape as crashes instead of in-band ok:false payloads and wrap them at the tool boundary on the call_tool precedent (mag/mcp_server.py:309-329); landing spot: tools/__init__.py call paths, one tool per sitting.
rows.falsifier: A tool failure surfaces as process or transport death with no in-band record any caller could have branched on.

rows.law: payload refs are serialized params, not cached results
rows.claim: A fan-in payload ref is a replay descriptor carrying the original tool name plus arguments, not cached server state, so N prior calls merge into one consumer with no shared session and the chain stays stable across schema drift in surrounding fields.
rows.quote:
refs are portable because they are serialized
call parameters, so fan-in is N prior calls merged into 1 consumer without any shared
session state.
rows.steal: One seat one sitting: convert one fold or handoff from sharing transcript state to passing the named output file plus the producing command as the descriptor; landing spot: workflow pass-off asks (workflow_gate interagent check: outputs feed later asks), one workflow per sitting.
rows.falsifier: A consumer can only reproduce upstream work from live shared session state and fails when handed only the descriptor (outputs plus producing command).

rows.law: three-ring auth with broker-issued authority for mutating calls
rows.claim: Authorization is a ring gradient (ring 0 stdio spawn-is-trust, ring 1 LAN shared key constant-time compare, ring 2 internet per-seat tokens) and a mutating call executes only inside a broker authority envelope; prompt text proposes, only switchboard-issued authority executes, and provider keys never cross.
rows.quote:
an external agent's PROMPT can
propose a bank; only an authority object issued through the switchboard
executes it.
rows.steal: One seat one sitting: before exposing any estate mutating verb to a remote surface, write its ring and authority path into the manifest row (bridge ROLE_TOOLSETS profile, effect_broker execute envelope per mcp-bridge.md section 5.3, effect_broker.py:205-219); landing spot: the bridge profile design review, one tool per sitting.
rows.falsifier: A mutating effect executes on the strength of a model or prompt message with no switchboard-issued authority object anywhere in its receipt chain.
